summary.text: If your MediSave is not enough, family savings and Government assistance may help.

details.heading: Use family MediSave
details.body: If your MediSave account is depleted, you may use your spouse's MediSave for long-term care withdrawals. You may use your family members' MediSave for other healthcare treatments.

details.heading: Apply for assistance
details.body: You may apply for means-tested Government assistance schemes, such as ElderFund and the Home Caregiving Grant, for long-term care costs.

details.heading: Other help if needed
details.body: If you still cannot pay after Government subsidies and other support, MediFund and ComCare may help.

example_phrasings: What if I have insufficient MediSave balances for my healthcare and long-term care expenses?
What can I do if my MediSave is not enough?
Can my family help pay for my care?

sources.page_title: What if I have insufficient MediSave balances for my healthcare and long-term care expenses?

quotes.text: If you have depleted your MediSave account, you may tap on your spouse's MediSave for long-term care withdrawals, and your family members' MediSave for your other healthcare treatments.
You may also apply for other forms of assistance such as means-tested Government assistance schemes (ElderFund, Home Caregiving Grant) to meet your long-term care costs needs.
If you are still unable to pay for your care even after Government subsidies and other means of support, there are other forms of assistance such as MediFund and ComCare.
